applicable_when: The current B-tile load uses manual scalar pointer arithmetic to load B as [BLOCK_N, BLOCK_K] then calls tl.trans() to get [BLOCK_K, BLOCK_N] for tl.dot. Even though the global load is coalesced (K is stride-1), Triton's backend must stage the transposed tile through shared memory for tl.dot. The resulting shared memory layout has BLOCK_N=64 as the fast dimension with stride 1, causing 8-way bank conflicts (64 floats x 4 bytes = 256 bytes = 8 x 32-byte banks). Replacing the manual pointer arithmetic + tl.trans() with tl.make_block_ptr(..., order=(0, 1)) tells the Triton backend that the B tile is column-major (K is the fast/contiguous dim in the tile), allowing it to lay out shared memory with K as the innermost dimension and eliminating the bank conflict pattern. The block_ptr approach also enables the compiler to use async copy instructions (cp.async) which overlap global-to-shared transfers with compute, further hiding the MIO latency that currently causes 59.5% of stalls.
